# requireNonEmptyString

<link-summary>Returns the value as a string that carries something, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonEmptyString() — Returns the value as a string that carries something, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonEmptyString(value: string | null | undefined, message?: string): string;
```

Whitespace does not count as content: a string of spaces fails the check just as an empty one does. This is the guard most of the string helpers in this library open with.

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type                          | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                | `string \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`                      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same string.

## Throws

| Exception              | Condition                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `EmptyStringException` | the value is not a string, or holds nothing but whitespace. |

## Examples

### In use

```javascript
requireNonEmptyString("Data"); // => "Data"
requireNonEmptyString("   "); // throws EmptyStringException
```
